body:
For the curiosity exercise I had to put the capstone aside, which was probably useful because otherwise I would have ended up writing forty versions of the proposal question. The questions went everywhere: AI, NPC personalities, why NPCs need limits, AI that knows me better than me, AI as a friend, who decides AI morals, games, immersion, making computers, operating systems, the universe, Christ, blacksmithing, craft, originality, business, writing, health and how I organise my thoughts.

Some of it is clearly not this capstone. I like building things and there are a lot of things I want to know how to make in my life. That does not mean all of them are secretly part of one project.

The thing that started mattering was what survived after asking why over and over. 

One question was: Are we not addicted to letting something be useful and taking over for efficiency than allowing authorship?

That one kept going. People made AI to be useful, not dangerous. We corrupt technology and then blame the technology. AI can make people hand over authorship of their own ideas. I grew up aiming for perfection but perfection is impossible because people are too imperfect. Efficiency can be an asset but it can also be what makes someone ordinary. How do you use a tool for authenticity without letting the tool become the whole personality? Why has being “better” become doing something faster? Do the things we think make us human actually make us original or just less efficient? I want efficiency and I also want originality, and those two do not always sit comfortably together.

Another chain that became more important than I expected was around writing and thought:
- I think faster than I can explain.
- I struggle translating thoughts sometimes.
- People curate their thinking before it even touches paper.
- What does unfiltered thinking reveal?
- How much do we restrict our own thinking so someone else can understand it?
- Does doing that make us more predictable?
- Why does everybody have to understand my thought process in one straight direction?
- Why can two things not be true at once?
- Why does everything keep becoming one side or the other?
